title: Masala Oats with Scrambled Egg
description: Spiced Indian-style oats cooked with tomato and spinach, topped with soft scrambled eggs. High-protein twist on a classic breakfast.
instructions: Heat 5g olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add chopped tomato and spinach; sauté 2–3 minutes until wilted.
Add oats with 200ml water and cook, stirring, for 4–5 minutes until thick.
Season with salt and black pepper.
In a separate pan, scramble the eggs in the remaining 3g olive oil until just set.
Serve oats topped with scrambled eggs.
meal_prep_notes: Oats can be batch-cooked and refrigerated for 2 days; eggs are best made fresh.
chef_tips: Add a pinch of turmeric and cumin seeds (once available) for authentic masala flavour.

title: Greek Yogurt Power Bowl
description: Creamy Greek yogurt layered with rolled oats, ripe banana and crunchy almonds. A no-cook, high-protein breakfast ready in 3 minutes.
instructions: Slice the banana.
Layer Greek yogurt in a bowl.
Top with oats, banana slices and almonds.
Mix lightly and eat immediately, or refrigerate overnight for overnight oats style.
meal_prep_notes: Prep the night before for a grab-and-go breakfast. Add banana fresh in the morning to prevent browning.
chef_tips: Drizzle honey (5g) on top if extra sweetness is needed. Swap almonds for any other nut.

title: Egg and Veggie Scramble
description: Three-egg scramble loaded with bell pepper, spinach and tomato. A fast, lean, high-protein breakfast that keeps you full all morning.
instructions: Dice the bell pepper and tomato; roughly chop the spinach.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add bell pepper; sauté 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add tomato and spinach; cook 1 minute until wilted.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper, pour over the vegetables.
Stir gently until just set. Remove from heat while still slightly glossy.
meal_prep_notes: Best made fresh. Chop vegetables the night before to save time.
chef_tips: Do not overcook — pull off heat while eggs look slightly underdone; residual heat finishes them.

title: Chicken Quinoa Morning Bowl
description: Leftover grilled chicken served over warm quinoa with baby spinach and tomato. Unconventional but excellent for high-protein muscle gain mornings.
instructions: Cook quinoa: rinse 70g quinoa, add 140ml water, bring to boil then simmer covered 12 minutes.
Season and grill or pan-fry chicken breast until cooked through (internal 75°C). Slice.
Wilt spinach in the pan for 1 minute.
Assemble: quinoa base, spinach, sliced chicken, diced tomato.
Drizzle with lemon juice and season.
meal_prep_notes: Cook quinoa and chicken in batches on Sunday for the week.
chef_tips: Cold leftover chicken works perfectly here — just slice and place on warm quinoa.

title: Sweet Potato and Egg Hash
description: Crispy diced sweet potato hash cooked with bell pepper and spinach, topped with two sunny-side-up eggs. Carb-rich and filling.
instructions: Dice sweet potato into 1cm cubes.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add sweet potato and cook 12–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and tender.
Add diced bell pepper; cook 3 more minutes.
Add spinach and stir until wilted.
Push vegetables to the side and crack eggs into the pan. Cook sunny-side up 3 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper; serve immediately.
meal_prep_notes: Par-cook sweet potato in microwave (5 min) to halve pan time.
chef_tips: Covering the pan with a lid helps cook egg whites without flipping.

title: Tofu and Spinach Scramble
description: Crumbled firm tofu scrambled with spinach, tomato and garlic — a vegan alternative to scrambled eggs that is high in protein and iron.
instructions: Press tofu between paper towels for 5 minutes to remove excess moisture. Crumble with hands.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic; sauté 30 seconds.
Add crumbled tofu; cook 5–6 minutes, stirring, until golden.
Add spinach, tomato and bell pepper; cook 3 more minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper. Add lemon juice to finish.
meal_prep_notes: Can be prepped and refrigerated for 3 days. Reheat in pan.
chef_tips: Add a pinch of turmeric for a golden egg-like colour.

title: Oats Banana Smoothie Bowl
description: Thick blended oats-and-banana bowl topped with almonds and Greek yogurt. Naturally sweet, filling and packed with slow-release carbs.
instructions: Soak oats in 100ml water for 5 minutes (or use rolled oats which need no soaking).
Blend soaked oats with banana until smooth and thick.
Pour into a bowl.
Dollop Greek yogurt on top.
Sprinkle chopped almonds.
Eat immediately.
meal_prep_notes: Blend the oat-banana base the night before and refrigerate; add toppings fresh.
chef_tips: Use a frozen banana for a thicker, colder smoothie bowl without ice.

title: Dal and Roti Breakfast Bowl
description: Wholesome Indian breakfast of cooked yellow lentils (dal) paired with whole-wheat roti. High in plant protein and complex carbs.
instructions: Rinse dal (lentils) under cold water.
Pressure cook or boil dal with 250ml water and pinch of salt for 15–20 minutes until soft.
Heat 5g olive oil in a small pan; add chopped garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Add chopped tomato and spinach; cook 3 minutes.
Stir the tomato mixture into the dal; simmer 5 minutes.
Serve with warm roti.
meal_prep_notes: Dal keeps for 4 days in fridge and freezes well. Make a large batch.
chef_tips: A squeeze of lemon juice before serving brightens the flavour dramatically.

title: Avocado and Egg Roti Toast
description: Indian fusion take on avocado toast — creamy smashed avocado and two boiled eggs on a warm whole-wheat roti. Healthy fats meet quality protein.
instructions: Hard-boil or poach the eggs (8 minutes boiling for hard boil).
Warm the roti in a dry pan or directly on a gas flame.
Halve the avocado; remove flesh and smash with a fork.
Season smashed avocado with lemon juice, salt and black pepper.
Spread avocado over the warm roti.
Top with sliced egg, diced tomato and a final squeeze of lemon.
meal_prep_notes: Boil eggs in advance and refrigerate for up to 5 days.
chef_tips: Add a pinch of chili flakes on the avocado for heat (once in DB).

title: Quinoa Yogurt Breakfast Bowl
description: Warm cooked quinoa mixed with Greek yogurt and topped with banana and almonds. Excellent protein and amino acid profile from two complete protein sources.
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly. Combine with 160ml water in a saucepan.
Bring to boil, then reduce heat to low, cover and cook 12 minutes until water absorbed.
Let stand 3 minutes; fluff with fork.
Allow to cool slightly (2 minutes) then stir in Greek yogurt.
Top with sliced banana and chopped almonds.
meal_prep_notes: Cook quinoa in batches and refrigerate. Warm slightly before mixing with yogurt.
chef_tips: A drizzle of honey (5g) makes this taste like dessert while keeping it nutritious.

title: Grilled Chicken Brown Rice Bowl
description: Classic high-protein lunch — juicy grilled chicken breast over steamed brown rice with broccoli and a lemon-garlic drizzle.
instructions: Cook brown rice: combine 75g raw rice with 180ml water; bring to boil, cover, simmer 35 minutes.
Season chicken with salt, pepper and minced garlic.
Grill or pan-fry chicken 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest 3 minutes, then slice.
Steam or microwave broccoli 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Assemble bowl: rice base, broccoli, sliced chicken.
Drizzle with lemon juice and 5g olive oil.
meal_prep_notes: Make 4 portions at once — keeps 4 days in fridge. Just reheat rice and chicken together.
chef_tips: Marinate chicken in garlic + lemon juice for 30 minutes before cooking for deeper flavour.

title: Chicken Quinoa Power Salad
description: Mediterranean-inspired warm quinoa salad with grilled chicken, cucumber, tomato and spinach, dressed with lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Cook quinoa (dry 70g) with 140ml water for 12 minutes. Fluff and cool slightly.
Grill chicken breast with salt, pepper and 5g olive oil until cooked. Slice into strips.
Combine warm quinoa with spinach (spinach will wilt slightly from heat).
Add diced tomato, sliced cucumber.
Top with chicken strips.
Dress with lemon juice and remaining olive oil. Toss gently.
meal_prep_notes: Keep dressing separate until ready to eat. Keeps 3 days in fridge.
chef_tips: Add a pinch of black pepper and garlic to the dressing for more complexity.

title: Dal Tadka with Brown Rice
description: Classic North Indian yellow dal tempered with ginger and garlic, served with steamed brown rice. High in plant protein and fibre.
instructions: Rinse 100g dal lentils and pressure cook or boil with 300ml water and pinch of salt until soft (15–20 min).
Cook 75g brown rice with 180ml water (30–35 min).
In a small pan, heat olive oil. Add minced garlic and grated ginger; cook 1 minute.
Add diced tomato and spinach; cook 3–4 minutes until tomato softens.
Pour the tadka (tempering) over the cooked dal and stir well.
Simmer dal 5 minutes. Serve over or alongside brown rice.
meal_prep_notes: Dal keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well for 3 months.
chef_tips: A squeeze of lemon before serving lifts the whole dish. Add cumin seeds to the tadka oil once available.

title: Tofu Stir-Fry with Brown Rice
description: Crispy tofu cubes with broccoli and bell pepper in a garlic-ginger stir-fry sauce, served over steamed brown rice.
instructions: Press tofu 10 minutes to remove moisture. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Cook brown rice (70g dry) with 170ml water.
Heat 5g olive oil in a wok or large pan over high heat. Add tofu cubes and fry 5–7 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add remaining oil, garlic and ginger; stir-fry 30 seconds.
Add broccoli florets and bell pepper; stir-fry 4–5 minutes on high heat.
Add spinach; cook 1 minute until wilted.
Return tofu; toss everything together. Season with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
Serve over brown rice.
meal_prep_notes: Keep rice, tofu-veggie stir-fry separate. Reheat wok-style on high for best texture.
chef_tips: Pat tofu very dry before frying — this is the key to getting it crispy, not soggy.

title: Salmon Quinoa Bowl
description: Pan-seared salmon over quinoa with fresh spinach, cucumber and tomato. Rich in omega-3s and complete protein.
instructions: Cook quinoa (70g dry) with 140ml water. Set aside.
Season salmon fillet with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
Heat 5g olive oil in a pan over medium-high. Cook salmon 3–4 minutes skin-side down, then flip and cook 2–3 more minutes until flaking.
Arrange quinoa in a bowl; layer with spinach, sliced cucumber and diced tomato.
Place salmon on top. Drizzle remaining olive oil and lemon juice over.
meal_prep_notes: Salmon is best cooked fresh. Quinoa and veg can be prepped a day ahead.
chef_tips: Rest salmon 1 minute before plating. Do not overcook — it should still be slightly translucent in the centre.

title: Egg Fried Brown Rice
description: Wok-tossed brown rice with three eggs, broccoli and bell pepper in a garlic-based sauce. Comfort food that is actually nutritious.
instructions: Cook brown rice (80g dry) ahead of time; spread on a tray and refrigerate if possible (day-old rice fries better).
Beat eggs with a pinch of salt.
Heat 5g olive oil in a wok over high heat. Scramble eggs quickly; remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil, garlic and ginger; stir-fry 30 seconds.
Add broccoli and bell pepper; stir-fry 4 minutes.
Add rice; stir-fry 3 minutes on high heat, pressing against pan to get slight char.
Return eggs; toss everything together.
Finish with green onion and black pepper.
meal_prep_notes: Use leftover rice from previous day for best results.
chef_tips: High heat is essential — do not crowd the pan.

ingredients.preparation_notes: dry weight, ideally day-old cooked rice

title: Mediterranean Chicken Roti Wrap
description: Grilled chicken with tzatziki-style Greek yogurt, cucumber, tomato and spinach wrapped in a warm whole-wheat roti.
instructions: Season chicken with garlic, salt, black pepper and 5g lemon juice. Grill or pan-fry 6–7 minutes per side.
Mix Greek yogurt with remaining lemon juice, salt and minced garlic for the sauce.
Warm roti on a dry pan 30 seconds per side.
Spread yogurt sauce over roti.
Layer spinach, sliced cucumber, tomato and sliced chicken.
Roll tightly and serve immediately.
meal_prep_notes: Cook chicken ahead. Wrap just before eating to prevent sogginess.
chef_tips: Toast the roti slightly for a crispier texture.

title: Dal Khichdi
description: A comforting one-pot Indian dish of rice and lentils cooked together with ginger, garlic and spinach. Easy to digest and perfectly balanced.
instructions: Rinse brown rice and dal together.
In a pot, heat olive oil; add garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute.
Add diced tomato; cook 2 minutes.
Add rinsed rice and dal; stir to coat.
Add 400ml water and spinach; bring to boil.
Cover and cook on low heat 30 minutes until everything is soft and porridge-like.
Season with salt. Serve hot with a drizzle of lemon juice.
meal_prep_notes: Khichdi thickens as it cools — add a splash of water when reheating.
chef_tips: The perfect khichdi has the consistency of thick porridge — if it is too dry, add more water.

title: Grilled Chicken and Avocado Salad
description: Simple, low-carb salad with grilled chicken breast, creamy avocado, fresh cucumber and baby spinach dressed in lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Grill or pan-fry chicken breast seasoned with salt, pepper and garlic. Slice.
Halve and cube the avocado.
Combine spinach, sliced cucumber, diced tomato and avocado in a bowl.
Top with sliced chicken.
Whisk together olive oil and lemon juice; drizzle over salad.
Season with salt and black pepper. Serve immediately.
meal_prep_notes: Add avocado just before eating to prevent browning. Keep dressing separate.
chef_tips: Grill chicken over high heat to get good char marks — adds flavour.

title: Quinoa Lentil Power Bowl
description: A vegan high-protein bowl combining quinoa and red lentils with roasted sweet potato, spinach and tomato.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss diced sweet potato with 5g olive oil and salt; roast 20–25 minutes until golden.
Cook quinoa (60g dry) with 120ml water for 12 minutes.
Cook dal lentils (50g dry) in 200ml water for 15 minutes until tender.
Wilt spinach in a pan with 3g olive oil; add diced tomato and bell pepper.
Combine quinoa, lentils, sweet potato and vegetables.
Dress with lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
meal_prep_notes: All components keep 4 days refrigerated. Assemble fresh.
chef_tips: Add garlic to the lentils while cooking for extra depth.

title: Tofu and Sweet Potato Curry
description: Indian-spiced tofu and sweet potato cooked in a tomato-spinach base. A hearty vegan meal with plant protein and slow-release carbs.
instructions: Press and cube tofu. Pan-fry in 5g olive oil until golden (5–6 min). Remove.
In the same pan, add remaining oil, garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute.
Add diced sweet potato; cook 5 minutes stirring.
Add diced tomato; cook 3 minutes until soft.
Add spinach and 100ml water; stir and cover. Cook 10 minutes until sweet potato is tender.
Return tofu; stir gently to combine.
Season with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
meal_prep_notes: Keeps 4 days refrigerated. Tastes better the next day as flavours develop.
chef_tips: Add a pinch of turmeric and coriander powder (once available) for authentic curry taste.

title: Salmon and Brown Rice Bowl
description: Pan-seared salmon over steamed brown rice with sliced avocado, cucumber and spinach — a Japanese donburi-inspired bowl.
instructions: Cook brown rice (75g dry) with 180ml water for 30–35 minutes.
Season salmon with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
Pan-sear salmon in 5g olive oil: 3–4 minutes per side until skin is crispy and flesh flakes easily.
Arrange rice in a bowl. Add sliced cucumber, avocado and spinach.
Flake salmon on top.
Drizzle with remaining olive oil and lemon juice.
meal_prep_notes: Cook rice ahead; salmon is best cooked fresh.
chef_tips: Rest salmon 1 minute before flaking. A drop of ginger juice adds a nice finish.

title: Tofu Quinoa Buddha Bowl
description: A complete vegan meal — crispy tofu, warm quinoa, roasted sweet potato and steamed broccoli with a zesty lemon dressing.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cube sweet potato, toss with 4g olive oil and salt. Roast 25 minutes.
Cook quinoa (70g dry) in 140ml water. Set aside.
Press and cube tofu. Pan-fry in 4g olive oil until golden, ~5–6 minutes. Season.
Steam broccoli florets 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Assemble bowl: quinoa, sweet potato, broccoli and tofu.
Drizzle with remaining olive oil and lemon juice.
meal_prep_notes: Prep all components separately. Assembles in 2 minutes at meal time.
chef_tips: Season each component individually for best flavour rather than seasoning the assembled bowl.

title: Baked Chicken with Sweet Potato and Broccoli
description: One-tray dinner of herb-seasoned chicken breast, roasted sweet potato wedges and broccoli. Minimal effort, maximum nutrition.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut sweet potato into wedges. Toss with 5g olive oil and salt.
Place chicken breast on the tray; rub with garlic, salt, black pepper and 5g olive oil.
Add sweet potato wedges and broccoli florets around the chicken.
Bake 25–30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Rest chicken 3 minutes; squeeze lemon juice over everything before serving.
meal_prep_notes: Make 3 trays at once for the week. Refrigerate up to 4 days.
chef_tips: Use a meat thermometer — it takes the guesswork out of chicken doneness.

title: Pan-Seared Salmon with Quinoa and Spinach
description: Restaurant-quality dinner ready in 20 minutes. Crispy-skinned salmon on a bed of fluffy quinoa with wilted garlic spinach.
instructions: Cook quinoa (80g dry) with 160ml water for 12 minutes. Fluff.
Pat salmon dry. Season with salt and black pepper.
Heat 5g olive oil in pan over high heat until shimmering. Place salmon skin-side down; press gently.
Cook 4 minutes without moving, then flip and cook 2–3 more minutes.
In same pan, add garlic and spinach with 3g olive oil; wilt 2 minutes.
Plate quinoa, top with garlicky spinach and salmon.
Finish with lemon juice, tomato and a pinch of black pepper.
meal_prep_notes: Quinoa can be cooked ahead. Salmon must be cooked fresh.
chef_tips: Starting skin-side down on high heat gives you the crispiest skin.

title: Chicken Broccoli Stir-Fry with Brown Rice
description: Quick weeknight stir-fry with tender chicken, crisp broccoli and bell pepper over steamed brown rice.
instructions: Cook brown rice (80g dry) with 200ml water for 30 minutes.
Slice chicken breast into thin strips. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 5g olive oil in wok over high heat. Stir-fry chicken strips 4–5 minutes until cooked. Remove.
Add 5g olive oil, garlic and ginger to wok; stir-fry 30 seconds.
Add broccoli and bell pepper; stir-fry on high heat 4 minutes.
Return chicken; toss everything together.
Season with lemon juice, salt and black pepper. Serve over rice.
meal_prep_notes: Make 3 servings at once. Keeps 4 days in fridge.
chef_tips: Slice chicken thinly — 5mm strips cook through quickly and stay juicy.

title: Dal and Roti Dinner
description: The quintessential Indian dinner — thick spiced yellow dal with two whole-wheat rotis and wilted spinach. Simple and deeply nourishing.
instructions: Wash 100g dal; boil with 300ml water and pinch of salt until soft (20 min) or pressure cook.
Heat 8g olive oil in a pan. Add garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute.
Add tomato; cook 3–4 minutes until pulpy.
Add spinach; wilt 2 minutes.
Pour tadka into cooked dal; simmer 5 minutes. Season.
Serve with 2 warm rotis (120g).
meal_prep_notes: Batch cook dal for the week. Rotis are best freshly made or warmed.
chef_tips: The more you let the dal simmer with the tadka, the better it tastes.

title: Chicken Quinoa Mediterranean Bowl
description: Herb-marinated grilled chicken over fluffy quinoa with cucumber, tomato and spinach — clean, filling and rich in micronutrients.
instructions: Marinate chicken in lemon juice, garlic, salt and black pepper for 10–30 minutes.
Cook quinoa (80g dry) with 160ml water for 12 minutes. Fluff.
Grill marinated chicken 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through. Slice.
Wilt spinach in a dry pan 1–2 minutes.
Assemble: quinoa, spinach, diced tomato, sliced cucumber, sliced chicken.
Drizzle with olive oil and any remaining lemon juice.
meal_prep_notes: Marinate chicken overnight in fridge for deeper flavour.
chef_tips: Let chicken rest 5 minutes before slicing to keep it juicy.

title: Egg Spinach Quinoa Bowl
description: Soft-boiled eggs on a warm quinoa and wilted spinach base with fresh tomato. A vegetarian dinner with complete protein.
instructions: Cook quinoa (80g dry) with 160ml water for 12 minutes.
Soft-boil eggs 6–7 minutes; peel and halve.
Heat olive oil and garlic in a pan; add spinach and wilt 2 minutes.
Combine warm quinoa with wilted spinach.
Top with halved soft-boiled eggs and fresh diced tomato.
Season with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
meal_prep_notes: Quinoa and spinach can be prepped ahead. Boil eggs fresh.
chef_tips: A 6.5-minute boil gives a jammy yolk — perfect for a bowl.

title: Tofu Dal Curry
description: Protein-dense Indian curry combining firm tofu with red lentils, tomato and garlic spinach. Surprisingly filling and satisfying.
instructions: Press and cube tofu; pan-fry in 5g olive oil until golden. Remove and set aside.
In same pan, heat 3g olive oil; fry garlic and ginger 1 minute.
Add diced tomato; cook 3 minutes until soft.
Add rinsed dal and 250ml water; bring to boil. Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Add spinach; cook 3 more minutes.
Stir in tofu; simmer 5 minutes. Season with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
Serve as a thick curry — pair with roti or quinoa if higher calories needed.
meal_prep_notes: Flavour improves overnight. Make a double batch.
chef_tips: Add turmeric and coriander (once available) to the garlic step for a proper curry base.

title: Grilled Lamb with Roasted Zucchini and Quinoa
description: Herb-marinated lamb with roasted zucchini and fluffy quinoa — a Mediterranean-style high-protein dinner for non-vegetarians wanting variety.
instructions: Marinate lamb leg (150g) in garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, salt and black pepper for 15–30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Slice zucchini; toss with 4g olive oil and salt. Roast 20 minutes until golden.
Cook quinoa (80g dry) with 160ml water.
Grill or pan-sear lamb 4 minutes per side for medium. Rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Assemble: quinoa base, roasted zucchini and spinach, sliced lamb.
Drizzle with remaining lemon juice.
meal_prep_notes: Marinate lamb the night before. Quinoa and zucchini can be prepped ahead.
chef_tips: Lamb is best served slightly pink inside. Do not overcook.

title: Chicken Dal Dinner
description: Hearty Indian non-vegetarian dinner combining grilled chicken and thick lentil dal. A protein-packed combination eaten across North India.
instructions: Cook dal lentils (80g dry) in 250ml water until soft. Season.
Grill or pan-fry chicken breast (150g) with garlic, salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a small pan; fry garlic and ginger 1 minute.
Add tomato and spinach; cook 4 minutes.
Stir this tadka into the dal; simmer 5 minutes.
Serve dal alongside sliced chicken. Add lemon juice over both.
meal_prep_notes: Cook dal in a big batch. Grill chicken on the day.
chef_tips: Season both the dal and the chicken assertively — they are a pairing and need to balance each other.

title: Salmon and Avocado Dinner Salad
description: A light but protein-rich evening meal — pan-seared salmon with creamy avocado, fresh vegetables and a lemon dressing. Low carb, high in healthy fats.
instructions: Pan-sear salmon (180g) in 5g olive oil, 3–4 minutes per side. Season with salt and black pepper.
While salmon cooks, cube avocado flesh and slice cucumber.
Arrange spinach, cucumber, tomato and avocado in a wide bowl.
Place salmon (whole or flaked) on top.
Whisk remaining olive oil with lemon juice; drizzle over.
Season and serve immediately.
meal_prep_notes: Prepare the vegetables ahead. Cook salmon just before eating.
chef_tips: Do not move the salmon while cooking — let the crust form before flipping.

title: Zucchini Chicken Skillet
description: One-skillet dinner of sliced chicken breast with sautéed zucchini, bell pepper and garlic in olive oil. Fast, clean and low-carb.
instructions: Slice chicken into strips; season with salt, pepper and garlic.
Heat 5g olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken strips 5–6 minutes until cooked through. Remove.
Add 5g olive oil to the same skillet. Add sliced zucchini and bell pepper; sauté 5–6 minutes until tender.
Add spinach; wilt 1 minute.
Return chicken; toss to combine.
Finish with lemon juice and black pepper.
meal_prep_notes: Keeps 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over medium heat for best texture.
chef_tips: Don't overcrowd the pan — cook chicken in batches if needed for proper browning.

title: Brown Rice Egg Fried Rice
description: Wok-fried brown rice with three eggs, broccoli, bell pepper and spring onion. A vegetarian dinner that comes together in 15 minutes.
instructions: Cook brown rice (100g dry) ahead of time; spread on a plate and chill if possible.
Heat 5g olive oil in wok over high heat. Beat and scramble eggs, then remove and set aside.
Add 5g olive oil, garlic and ginger; stir-fry 30 seconds.
Add broccoli and bell pepper; stir-fry on high 4–5 minutes.
Add rice; stir-fry 3 minutes pressing against wok sides.
Return eggs and toss everything together.
Garnish with sliced green onion; season with salt and black pepper.
meal_prep_notes: Day-old refrigerated rice gives the best texture for fried rice.
chef_tips: Never add cold water to a wok stir-fry — it kills the heat and makes things soggy.

title: Dal Quinoa Power Dinner
description: A complete vegan dinner — spiced red lentils over quinoa with wilted spinach and fresh tomato. Excellent protein-to-calorie ratio.
instructions: Cook quinoa (80g dry) with 160ml water for 12 minutes.
Cook dal lentils (80g dry) in 250ml water until soft (15–20 min). Drain excess water.
Heat olive oil; fry garlic and ginger 1 minute. Add tomato and spinach; cook 4 minutes.
Mix the garlic-tomato mixture into the cooked dal. Simmer 5 minutes.
Serve dal over quinoa.
Season with salt, black pepper and lemon juice.
meal_prep_notes: Both quinoa and dal keep 4 days. Excellent meal prep recipe.
chef_tips: Add a drizzle of olive oil right at the end for a glossy finish.

title: Greek Yogurt and Almond Bowl
description: A quick high-protein snack — thick Greek yogurt with crunchy almonds and banana. Ready in 2 minutes.
instructions: Scoop Greek yogurt into a bowl.
Slice the banana and add on top.
Sprinkle chopped almonds.
Eat immediately.
meal_prep_notes: Portion yogurt and almonds in advance for quick grab-and-go.
chef_tips: Frozen banana makes this taste like ice cream. Excellent post-workout snack.

title: Avocado Roti Toast
description: Smashed avocado on warm roti with fresh tomato and lemon — an Indian-style quick snack that's filling and rich in healthy fats.
instructions: Warm roti on a dry pan 30 seconds per side.
Smash avocado flesh with a fork; season with lemon juice, salt and black pepper.
Spread smashed avocado over warm roti.
Top with diced tomato. Eat immediately.
meal_prep_notes: Prepare avocado fresh to prevent browning. Roti can be warmed ahead.
chef_tips: Use a ripe avocado — it should yield easily when pressed.

title: Boiled Eggs with Almonds
description: The simplest high-protein snack — three boiled eggs with a handful of almonds. Combines complete protein with healthy fats.
instructions: Place eggs in cold water; bring to boil, cook 8–9 minutes for hard boil.
Transfer eggs to ice water for 1 minute; peel.
Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Serve with almonds.
meal_prep_notes: Boil a batch of 6–8 eggs at start of the week. Keeps 5 days in fridge.
chef_tips: Adding a teaspoon of vinegar to the boiling water makes peeling easier.

title: Banana Almond Quinoa Snack Bowl
description: Warm quinoa with sliced banana and almonds — a surprisingly satisfying snack that doubles as a light breakfast.
instructions: Rinse and cook quinoa (60g dry) with 120ml water for 12 minutes.
While still warm, top with sliced banana and chopped almonds.
Eat warm or at room temperature.
meal_prep_notes: Cook a big batch of quinoa and portion into containers. Add banana fresh.
chef_tips: A drizzle of honey (5g) makes this taste indulgent. Add a pinch of cinnamon if available.

title: Greek Yogurt Cucumber Dip with Roti
description: A protein-rich Indian take on tzatziki — Greek yogurt with cucumber, garlic and lemon served as a dip with warm roti strips.
instructions: Grate cucumber; squeeze out excess water with a cloth.
Mix grated cucumber into Greek yogurt.
Add minced garlic, lemon juice, salt and black pepper. Stir.
Warm roti and cut into strips.
Serve yogurt dip alongside roti strips.
meal_prep_notes: Dip keeps 2 days refrigerated. Prepare roti fresh.
chef_tips: Squeezing water from cucumber is essential — otherwise the dip becomes watery.
